answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring each identity to grow a unique plume of original work that cannot be copied. The plume is checked against a willow of prior answers from the same author, so near-duplicates are rejected on the ledger. A wharf of independent graders then attests only the fresh strands. Forging many identities therefore costs one full original generation and external verification cycle per identity, not a single cheap template.
